Synopsis:
US and global airfares remain sharply elevated (+25–30% YoY) driven by a confluence of factors: a US-Iran war-driven jet fuel price spike (jet fuel ~$149/bbl, +65% YTD), reduced global refinery capacity, Boeing/Airbus delivery constraints, FAA staffing issues, and persistent travel demand. Airlines are passing through fuel costs under war-cover, and low-cost carrier exits (Spirit Airlines) are reducing competitive pressure. Even a ceasefire is unlikely to deliver near-term airfare relief, with normalization potentially taking 12+ months.

**Q03. Risks for increasing gas demand or decreasing gas supply?**
Relevance: IMPLICIT
The US-Iran conflict context implies ongoing geopolitical risk to Middle East energy supply chains broadly — a conflict of this scale could affect LNG shipping routes and regional gas supply security. Refinery tightness could also incentivize some gas-to-liquids substitution pressure. These are indirect signals only.
